title: Satellite machine learning measures inundation across 542,850 conserved wetland sites
summary: A Support Vector Machine classifier applied to Sentinel-2 and Dynamic World data in Google Earth Engine mapped surface-water inundation across 542,850 wetland-related Conservation Reserve Program and Wetlands Reserve Program sites from 2018 to 2024. Measurable inundation occurred on 44.20% of CRP and 76.62% of WRP lands, persisted longer on WRP and on longer-enrolled CRP lands, and tracked hydric soil distribution. Reported validation accuracy was 95.50% on a random 75/25 split of 50,000 labelled points (RF 96.18%), but samples were split at point level so spatial autocorrelation may inflate it, there was no field hydrological validation, and surface water alone does not show conservation benefit.
ai_technology: Support Vector Machine (compared with Random Forest and CART) classifying land cover and water from Sentinel-2 and Dynamic World inputs.

evidence.tested: Retrospective satellite classification with held-out 25% validation points, comparison of three classifiers and a qualitative visual check of inundation frequency.
evidence.unknown: No field hydrological validation; point-level split may inflate accuracy; optical imagery misses vegetated or cloud-covered water; inundation does not establish ecosystem benefit or program causation. The same group previously mapped inundation across all CRP lands (Scientific Reports, March 2026); this study's distinct contribution is the wetland-focused CRP versus WRP comparison with hydric soils.
evidence.ai_role: The SVM classifier learns water and land classes from Sentinel-2 bands and produces the seasonal inundation maps on which all program comparisons rest.

source_review.scope: Full article-in-press PDF read independently (abstract, methods, classifier comparison, validation, limitations); received 1 Apr, accepted 20 Nov, online 24 Nov 2026 (Crossref); no preprint found; the group's earlier all-CRP study (10.1038/s41598-026-45281-y) is not in the catalog; catalog duplicate check none.
